source_extracts.quote: (A)(1) Application for a certificate of title shall be made in a form prescribed by the registrar of motor vehicles and shall be sworn to before a notary public or other officer empowered to administer oaths. The application shall be filed with the clerk of any court of common pleas.
The seller must complete the “assignment of ownership” portion on the back of the title and have their signature(s) notarized. Then present it to the buyer to finalize the transfer.
Buyer – Completes page 2 of the BMV 3770 in its entirety and has their signature(s) notarized. All owners must complete the assignment.
Dual ownership requires both parties to be present unless a notarized power of attorney is provided. Social Security numbers for all parties are required. Photocopies of title are not accepted.
(a) Five dollars for each certificate of title that is not applied for within thirty days after the later of the assignment or delivery of the motor vehicle described in it.

(b) Eighteen dollars, or twenty-three dollars if a board of county commissioners adopts a resolution authorizing the increased fee for that county, for each certificate of title or duplicate certificate of title...

(1) Up to five dollars for any notarial act that is not an online notarization; (2) For an online notarization, up to thirty dollars. ... The fees charged under division (A) of this section shall not be calculated on a per signature basis.

An inspection of a passport, driver's license, government-issued nondriver identification card, or other form of government-issued identification with the signature or photograph of the individual, which is current or expired not more than three years before performance of the notarial act, and is satisfactory to the notary public
Alterations or erasures on a title will void the document
Ohio titles are issued by Clerk of Courts title offices, the BMV does not issue titles.

scope_rules.forbidden: claiming the BUYER must be present when the SELLER's title assignment is notarized
scope_rules.reason: BMV: only the seller's assignment on the title must be notarized; the buyer separately completes their form and has their own signature notarized. Never state both must sign before the same notary at the same moment.

scope_rules.forbidden: naming Lake County / Cuyahoga as a $23 county
scope_rules.reason: ORC 4505.09 lets counties adopt the increase; we have not verified which counties did. Copy says 'some counties' only.

scope_rules.forbidden: stating a store notary price other than $5 per signature
scope_rules.reason: Only the repo-verified $5.00 counter price is cleared.
Frank hard ban in prose, headings, PR bodies.

scope_rules.forbidden: time guarantees like 'two minutes', 'under three minutes', 'never fails'
'two forms of ID' or 'two photo IDs' for notarization
scope_rules.reason: ORC 147.50 requires satisfactory government-issued ID (photo or signature) for a standard notarial act; the two-form rule belongs to USPS Form 1583, not notarization.
